# B494 row (b): a WASI p1 hello module, exit code and stdout through the pod
image route (the first evidence item): k3sm image load/import was not usable without sudo (the node's runtime socket is
readable only by the daemon's own account) and the cluster registry refuses a push without its per-boot credential (401, the
credential file is _k3sm-only on the server). So the spike binaries travel as a native darwin/arm64 OCI image built in scratch
(go-containerregistry v0.22.1, one layer: /bin/wasmspike, /bin/wasmspike-rt, /wasm/*), pushed to a scratch registry on this
Mac (read-write on loopback, read-only GET/HEAD on the LAN address, plain HTTP), and pulled by the node's own Puller like any
registry image. image: <lan-ip>:5494/b494/spike@sha256:7b6d3cc7db928002aef8b8fbf2c108cf6f536fdf12c764d1cdaa6f0d853e1af0
confined: yes. pod b494-hello, uid 250 (_k3sm), sandbox_check(getpid())=1 reported by the process itself. The generated profile
file sits under the _k3sm-only runtime state dir; it was not readable without sudo (excluded), so its sha256 is NOT recorded.
First attempt: evicted by the node's NoExecute taint (TaintManagerEviction) until the pod tolerated that one taint by key+value;
then refused once by the node's disk-pressure pull gate (host volume below 3 GiB free, not caused by this run); then pulled.

## crilog
The container log file itself (under /var/log/pods, mode 0700 _k3sm) was not readable without sudo. The bytes above under
'## log' are served from it by the node's log endpoint (kubectl logs --timestamps): the guest's fd_write(1) line
'hello from a wasi p1 module under k3sm' is there between the host's stderr lines.

## verdict
PASS. proc_exit(7) in the guest -> the host process exits 7 -> containerStatuses[0].state.terminated.exitCode 7, reason Error.
Side observations: startedAt is null in the terminated state; no Created/Started events were emitted for this pod.
